time_convention: t = frame / 24; frame = round(t * 24); frame 0 = t 0
units: pixels and seconds only; no metric scale estimated
view: high, nearly top-down (bird's-eye) view of a sandy beach with a rocky headland (top right), shallow water / sea (bottom and right). Camera tilted slightly: vertical structures (boat mast, cabin) lean toward the image TOP, so the camera looks somewhat 'up-image'; lower image rows are closer to the camera.

camera.evidence: phase correlation of the cliff patch and of a shoreline patch against frame 0: max |shift| 0.08 px over all 72 frames (scripts/camera.py)
camera.duplicate_frames: frames 0 and 1 are identical (mean abs diff 0.05 grey levels, i.e. codec noise); everything is static between them, motion starts at frame 1->2
camera.perspective_cues: no horizon visible. Near-nadir view; ground (beach/sea surface) is roughly the image plane. Lower image = slightly nearer: boat hull length shrinks 348.6 px (frame 0-5) -> ~344-346 px (frames 40-62) as it moves up-left; bird's peak wingspan grows from 54.7 px (frame 5, y~388) to 56.3 px (frame 31, y~500) to 62.4 px (frame 54, y~600).

objects.name: bird
objects.description: single dark (black) flying bird, seen from above with wings spread; only animal in the scene
objects.visible_frames: 0-67 (partly cut by left edge at frames 0-1, by right edge at frame 67; absent 68-71)

Flaps wings: span across flight peaks at frames 5 (54.7 px), 31 (56.3 px), 54 (62.4 px); minima ~31.6 px (f24), ~34.6 px (f20), ~35.9 px (f46). Body length along flight ~25-30 px.
